text.p: The New Zealand dollar opened largely flat on Tuesday after buying out of the U.K. saw it surge briefly to US$0.6916 overnight.
The kiwi opened at US$0.6893/00, up a touch from its 0.6885/92 finish on Monday. On its Trade-Weighted Index the kiwi was up four to 67.71.
Dealers said the London buying was possibly a large player switching out of Australia and into New Zealand.

"Again, it was just one of these early London orders that go through far too quickly for their own good -- it means it goes a little bit further than it necessarily should. The various sellers who were out there in force over $0.6910 were able to take advantage of the spike and sell into it," a Wellington dealer said.
Weakness in the Australian unit helped to dissipate the kiwi's short-lived flirtation with the other side of 69 US cents.
The Australian dollar opened at US$0.7485/90, against its 0.7512/17 close (NZ time) on Monday, taking the NZ/Australian cross to NZ$0.9199/14 from around 0.9165.

"The kiwi/aussie has probably come close to reaching levels where it does represent quite good selling. Somewhere around 9250 you'd have to say is probably looking a fairly good place to sell kiwi against the aussie," one dealer said.

He said ongoing eurokiwi issuance meant traders were not too concerned about holding long positions on the kiwi, as the chances were there would be more buying out of London to cover euro settlements.
Dealers expected a range of US$0.6885-00 on the day, compared with the overnight range of 0.6889-16.

April retail trade data at 2245 GMT was expected to have little impact unless it was a rogue number, but with a range of -2.0 percent to +5.0 percent expected by the 11 economists polled by Reuters, it was difficult to pin down what would classify as "rogue".

The average forecast is for retail sales to rebound and rise 1.38 percent in April, following falls of 3.9 percent in March and 2.4 percent in February. Dealers said another sizeable fall would confirm the picture of a soft economy.
